root_cause.text: mm_drop_cid_on_cpu() did not validate that the CID is CPU-owned (ONCPU bit set), causing it to interpret a CID with the TRANSIT bit set as a valid CID and pass it to clear_bit, resulting in an out-of-bounds access.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "It invokes mm_drop_cid_on_cpu() which clears the not set ONCPU bit and then invokes clear_bit() with an insanely large bit number because TRANSIT is set (bit 29)." The patch adds a check `if (cid_on_cpu(pcp->cid))` before performing the CID drop, preventing the incorrect use of a CID that is not CPU-owned.

    sched/mmcid: Drop per CPU CID immediately when switching to per task mode
    
    When a exiting task initiates the switch from per CPU back to per task
    mode, it has already dropped its CID and marked itself inactive. But a
    leftover from an earlier iteration of the rework then reassigns the per
    CPU CID to the exiting task with the transition bit set.
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body contains a call to mm_drop_cid_on_cpu() at line 10737. No validation or guard is present in this function before the call; the comment only asserts that the CID does not have TRANSIT set but does not ensure the ONCPU bit or provide a safe fallback. Therefore, the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not applied in this code.
